title: Crypto misuse: wolfssl ECDH agree() does not explicitly validate peer public key on curve
description:
wolfssl_ecdh.c line 182: wc_ecc_import_x963_ex(..., peer_key, ctx->curve_id) followed immediately by wc_ecc_shared_secret() with no call to wc_ecc_check_key().

wolfCrypt analysis (ecc.c):
- wc_ecc_import_x963_ex() hardcodes untrusted=0 (line 11220), so the inline on-curve/infinity checks (block 2, lines 11043-11124) are NEVER executed.
- WOLFSSL_VALIDATE_ECC_IMPORT (the compile-time flag that would trigger wc_ecc_check_key() at import) defaults OFF. Not set in FIPS builds by default.
- _ecc_validate_public_key() (called by wc_ecc_check_key()) implements all four SP 800-56Ar3 §5.6.2.3.3 checks: not-infinity (line 10654), Qx/Qy in range (lines 10671-10683), on-curve y²=x³+ax+b (line 10690), order check n×Q=infinity (line 10696). These are ONLY reachable via wc_ecc_check_key().
- In default build: wc_ecc_import_x963_ex() does format parsing and coordinate deserialization ONLY. Zero SP 800-56A validation.

Fix: add wc_ecc_check_key(peer_key) after successful wc_ecc_import_x963_ex() at wolfssl_ecdh.c line 182. Treat any non-zero return as hard rejection.

Trigger: attacker supplies a peer public key not on the curve (or at infinity, or with order != n). wc_ecc_shared_secret() computes ECDH using the unchecked point. Small-subgroup attack can reduce Z entropy to near-zero without error signal.
close_reason: Added wc_ecc_check_key(peer_key) after wc_ecc_import_x963_ex in wolfssl_ecdh_agree — performs all 4 SP 800-56A §5.6.2.3.3 checks (not-infinity, range, on-curve, order)
